source_text: καὶ οὐδὲν εἰς τὸ ἐφεξῆς ταμιεύεται. Οὐδὲ ὑπολείπεταί τι τοῖς ἡδομένοις ἴχνος εὐφροσύνης ἢ λείψανον παρελθούσης τῆς κατὰ τὴν ἡδονὴν ἐνεργείας.
thought_title: No trace of gladness remains after pleasure passes
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that all such human activities end in vanity, now stating that nothing is stored up and no trace of gladness remains once the pleasurable activity has passed.
pass_a_gloss: And nothing is stored up for what comes next. Nor is any trace of gladness left behind for those who take pleasure, nor any remnant, once the activity according to pleasure has passed.

choices.why: The verb means to lay up or store away as in a treasury; 'stored up' keeps the sense of reserving for future use.
The verb means to remain or be left over; 'left behind' preserves the passive sense with the dative of the persons affected.
The present middle/passive participle of ἥδομαι means those experiencing pleasure; 'those who take pleasure' keeps the ongoing sense.
ἴχνος means a track or footprint; 'trace' captures the idea of a faint remaining mark.
λείψανον means a leftover or remains; 'remnant' keeps the sense of a small remaining piece.
The aorist participle of παρέρχομαι means having gone by or passed; 'has passed' keeps the temporal sense.

pass_b_english: Nothing is stored up for what comes next. Once the activity of pleasure has passed, no trace or remnant of gladness is left behind for those who took pleasure.
